beta_new:
On the first pitch, climb the face and faint crack up and left, then traverse left across Kreuser's Chimney into a horizontal crack. Follow it left to a vertical fingercrack and climb that to a ledge belay.

The second pitch goes up the face with two bolts to a thin crack leaning rightward, crosses it, and keeps on up the face above.

On the northeast flank, get over the rubble at the base, then follow the shallow trough worn smooth by water, clipping two bolts, to a small crack. Keeping to the trough's left side gives the 5.8 climbing.
Start twenty feet right of Rastaman Vibration and follow the broken crack and the face, clipping the one bolt, to the top of the slab.
West of the Sun Deck Boulder, climb the eighty-foot buttress facing south, beginning at its lower left and angling up and rightward. There is one bolt low on the route.
Start at the southeast-facing pillar and climb the arete that leans rightward, passing one bolt, to a horizontal crack. Move left to a ledge and finish up an easy hand crack.
Start at the left side of the white slab and climb the face, clipping three bolts, to the top.
Begin as Shalayly Direct does and follow that route to its third bolt, then descend a little and cross rightward past a bolt, making this a long girdle-style line.
Pitch one is a steep face, and a #1 Friend can ease the nerves at the eighth bolt. Once the bolts run out, pitch two is thinly protected though only 5.6, and most parties just run it out.
Midway up the south face, pass two replaced bolts to a sloping shelf. From there, aid past more bolts, under the overhang and then to the summit.

Stay mostly on the right side of the buttress dividing the south and east faces, moving leftward away from the corner system solely to reach the belay. From the belay, swing back round onto the east face and climb on until you spot the bolt.

Begin beside the big pine, on its right, and head diagonally rightward toward the conspicuous weak spot in the wall, then look for the bolts. A beeline to those bolts often turns out to be the wrong choice. Small wired nuts cover the opening moves.

Reach the tree from its right side, then climb the awkward hand crack right behind it, ending on a small platform. The second pitch traverses left from the ledge to a thin crack that leads to the summit, with micro-nuts protecting the crux friction moves.

On the first pitch climb the face, clipping two bolts, to a ledge, continue up the dihedral that faces right, over a little roof to another ledge, then move left to the belay. The second pitch climbs the face above, with four bolts, to the top.

Start at the foot of the buttress with three cracks that arch rightward, facing east, and climb the face immediately to the left of the leftmost crack. Take the easiest path; heading straight for the bolt makes it harder than the grade.
Follow the left-hand arete of the buttress straight up its seven bolts.
A short dihedral gets you started, then step right past a bolt to the base of the thin crack. Follow it past three fixed pins to a big ledge, where the face above leads to the top of the West Summit.
A brief, bolt-protected face section holds the crux and leads to a crack arching rightward. Follow that crack until you can move straight up the face over a horizontal crack to the top.

Climb a small dihedral until you can step right onto the face, then clip a bolt and slant rightward into a second vertical crack. Follow it to an alcove, take the crack and face above to a horizontal break with a bolt, and finish on small discontinuous cracks.
Follow the corner, which stays overhanging, clipping three bolts and a fixed pin on the way to the top. The name refers to the shallow dihedral formed by the upper corner.
Start in a finger seam and follow it up. The finish leaves a scoop and goes onto the face, passing one bolt.

Begin with a finger-width crack starting off a boulder and follow it up a steep runnel, clipping two or three bolts. Stay in the seam, where aluminum bashies help, as far as bolt three, then step right and finish by clipping the final bolt.
Climb the gentle slab to a flake with a single bolt, then angle up and rightward, clipping the second bolt, to the top.
Climb the face with one bolt to a thin crack, which holds the crux. Follow the crack leftward, clipping two fixed pitons, until you can join Dog Fight Giggle, then take its thin crack to the top.
Climb the arete alongside Kate's Fault, clipping two bolts on the way up. Gear is needed to build the belay.

Ascend roughly 45 feet of South Crack's upper pitch, then step left onto the arete and climb its face, clipping three bolts, to a horizontal crack. Reach right to clip the last bolt and go straight up from there; moving right after that clip makes it easier.
Start at an open book and climb the dihedral to a stance with a bolt. From there continue to a horizontal break and follow it rightward to a clear belay.

Take the thin crack system on the east face's right side up to a ledge, then keep going on the crack onto the face and past a bolt to a second ledge. Cross the face over a boulder, passing one more bolt, to the top.

Pitch one goes up a face to a crack and a pin under a bulge, with the belay in the alcove above it. Pitch two steps right of the vegetated crack onto the face and heads up to a bolt, with another runout beyond.

Pitch one follows a small crack, then traverses left to a bolt and goes past a catclaw tree to a crack and belay. Pitch two climbs the crack until it ends, face-climbs rightward and upward to a ramp and crack, follows the ramp to a horn, then steps left and finishes up a fingercrack.

The final pitch ascends a crack that arches rightward to the top.
Climb a dihedral and crack up to a belay on two bolts. Then step left and take an offwidth to a ramp leading to the summit, or take the steep, shallow crack on its left.

Climb the dihedral made by the flake's right side to a ledge, then carefully work up the fractured spike under the roof. Follow the roof crack leftward; at its end either bail leftward into the gully, or move right onto the face and clip two bolts.

Start on a pillar left of Edge, climb to a bolt, then shift left and climb to a ledge belay. The headwall above is tackled once you have clipped a bolt; the run-out section comes on the moves below the first bolt.
Parallel cracks lead to a flake crack and then a horizontal one. Move up to a bolt on the face, clip a second, and continue to the top, exiting rightward.
Climb the face, clipping two bolts, to a horizontal crack, then continue on the face past another bolt to ledges.
Take the detached flake, then make a delicate step left onto the face and go on to the upper face, passing a pair of fixed pins and one bolt. Two more bolts lead to the top.

Follow a crack of finger to hand size until it ends, then reach a bolt and head up the face to a broken section. Another bolt protects the face above and the step across the chasm; the top section is easy ground but unprotected.
Climb the face and detached flake until a step right gets you into a scoop. Then go up the face, drifting slightly rightward, clipping two bolts to the top.

Pitch one follows an obvious crack of hand and finger size until it ends, then moves left across the face past a bolt to the arete, merging with Indecent Exposure by its third clip. Pitch two is that route's upper part, to the summit.

Open with a crack and some face to a bolt, then angle up and rightward across the face, clipping three more, to the arete. Follow the arete past a horizontal crack and one more bolt; the angle eases near the top. Extra bolts were added to remove the original X rating.
Climb the face past the first bolt, where the crux sits, to gain a horizontal crack and the arete. Stay on the arete, clipping two more bolts, until you merge with Crater Maker.
